hints.title: Interval Boundary Character
hints.text: Partition palindromic subsequences by their outer enclosing characters among the four possibilities a, b, c, and d.

hints.title: Subproblem Intervals
hints.text: For each character ch, find its first and last occurrence within substring s[i...j]. If no such character exists, contribution is zero; if one, contribution is one; if two, contribution is two plus inner palindromes.

hints.title: Interval Recurrence
hints.text: Let memo(i, j) be distinct palindromic subsequences in s[i...j]. For each character x in abcd, find first occurrence l and last occurrence r. If l > r, add 0; if l == r, add 1; if l < r, add 2 + memo(l + 1, r - 1). Apply modulo 10^9 + 7.

hints.title: See the blueprint

complexity.notes: Interval dynamic programming enumerating first and last occurrences of the 4 characters.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Generating all subsequences and checking palindrome property takes exponential O(2^N) time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Memoizing (i, j) boundaries bounds states to O(N^2) with 4 transitions each.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Group palindromes by their boundary characters (a, b, c, d) to naturally eliminate duplicates.
